Redraw "building" with a visible trapdoor opening in the boardroom floor and the yellow hinge highlight called for in the brief — currently it reads as a filing cabinet or server rack, so the "floor drops away" beat doesn't land.

revisionNotes: Fix the trapdoor read: the executive is sprawled across the building top with legs crossing windows, reading as floating, not falling. Cut a visible trapdoor opening in the roof with the yellow hinge accent from the brief, and pose him dropping through it, legs below the roofline.

Lower the flag on its pole: it sits near the top of the canvas looking fully raised, contradicting the 'barely risen, quiet alarm' metaphor. Shorten the pole or move the flag to about a third up, inside the safe area.
Rebalance composition: the top half of the frame is nearly empty while everything crowds the bottom. Scale up the building/laptop/flagstack group and shift it upward to use the square more evenly.
Reattach the briefcase: it floats disconnected above the executive's hand. Tuck it closer at a smaller offset so the grip reads clearly.

review.verdict: The cast and metaphor are set up correctly (human exec, AI as laptop not robot), but the trapdoor/fall doesn't read clearly, the layout leaves the bottom third nearly empty while the top is cramped, and this blueprint split-scene look repeats too much of the recent batch — overall average falls below the pass bar.
revisionNotes: Render the trapdoor as an actual gap in the roof with the yellow hinge highlight the brief calls for — right now the executive is just pasted overlapping the building's window grid, which reads as a registration error, not a fall.

Flagstack prop currently reads as a plain filing box, not a 'tall stack of calendar pages' — add visible stacked page lines or date marks so the 'weeks of waiting' beat is legible without relying on the WEEKS LATER label.
Scale the briefcase up (it's nearly invisible at current size) and clean up the executive's pose so arms/legs don't cross through the building windows.
